source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Compare the preadmission, inpatient, and discharge medication lists and resolve discrepancies","B":"Copy the preadmission medication list without comparing inpatient or discharge changes","C":"Skip medication reconciliation after uncomplicated admissions because discrepancies are rare","D":"Leave discharge medication reconciliation entirely to pharmacy with no nursing involvement"}}
source_row.rationale: Discharge medication reconciliation involves systematically comparing the client's pre-admission medication list with medications ordered during the hospital stay and the final discharge medication list, to identify and resolve any discrepancies (omissions, duplications, dosing changes) before the client leaves, a critical patient safety process at this vulnerable transition point.
source_row.source_detail: Medication reconciliation at transitions: compare medication information and resolve discrepancies before transition/discharge; current NPSG framework; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: The Joint Commission — National Patient Safety Goals
source_row.stem: A nurse is preparing a client for discharge and performs medication reconciliation, and a colleague assumes this just means checking off the pre-admission list without comparing it to what was actually ordered during the stay. This process specifically instead involves:
